scenes.heading: Graphs of other non-linear relations
scenes.say: Not every graph is a line or a parabola. Today you will meet three new curves: exponentials, hyperbolas and circles, and learn to spot each one from its equation.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Savings that double, lollies shared, a dog on a lead
scenes.breaks: You can't share lollies among −2 friends, but a hyperbola includes negative x-values too.
scenes.say: Picture savings that double every week: slow at first, then explosive. That is an exponential. Twelve lollies shared among more and more friends: fewer each, but never zero. That is a hyperbola. And a dog on a three metre lead tied to a post traces a circle.

scenes.heading: Exponentials: y = 2ˣ
scenes.say: Here is y equals two to the power x. First it hugs the x-axis, then it passes through zero, one and doubles: two, four, eight. Its mirror image, two to the power negative x, falls instead. Neither ever touches the x-axis. That line is called an asymptote.
scenes.caption: y = 2ˣ hugs the x-axis, passes through (0, 1), then doubles: 2, 4, 8. Its mirror image y = 2⁻ˣ falls. Neither touches the x-axis: an asymptote.

scenes.heading: Hyperbolas: y = k/x
scenes.say: A hyperbola like y equals four over x has two separate branches. You cannot divide by zero, so it never touches either axis. With a positive k, the branches sit top right and bottom left. With negative k, top left and bottom right.
scenes.caption: A hyperbola like y = 4/x has two branches. You can't divide by zero, so it never touches the axes. Positive k: top right and bottom left. Negative k: top left and bottom right.

scenes.heading: Circles: x² + y² = r²
scenes.question: For x² + y² = 25, find the radius. Is (3, 4) on the circle?
scenes.say: A circle centred at the origin has equation x squared plus y squared equals r squared. For twenty-five, the radius is five. Test three, four: nine plus sixteen is twenty-five, so it is on the circle.
scenes.caption: x² + y² = r². For 25, the radius is 5. Test (3, 4): 9 + 16 = 25, so it is on the circle.

points: y = k/x: two branches, axes are asymptotes
x² + y² = r²: circle, radius r
Where x sits tells you the graph
scenes.say: Quick recap. Exponentials pass through zero, one and never touch the x-axis. Hyperbolas have two branches and never touch either axis. x squared plus y squared equals r squared is a circle of radius r. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Exponentials pass through (0, 1) and never touch the x-axis. Hyperbolas have two branches and never touch either axis. x² + y² = r² is a circle of radius r. Now try the practice questions!
